newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds declines comment on SMH sale. [CORRECTED 15:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Lloyds declines comment on SMH sale. [CORRECTED 15:20 GMT]

text.p: Lloyds TSB Group Plc on Monday would not comment on reports that it was considering the sale of its 96-percent-owned German private bank unit Schroeder, Muenchmeyer Hengst & Co (SMH).
"We never comment on market rumours," a spokesman for Lloyds said.
Earlier reports suggested Lloyds was set to sell the unit to an unspecified Swiss bank.
Lloyds stepped in to help SMH in the 1980's when the bank got into difficulties after one of its major clients, engineering group IBH, collapsed.

Last year, SMH announced it was withdrawing from lending business and would concentrate on investment banking activities such as institutional brokerage, asset management and retail securities business.
It said it planned to expand corporate finance and dealing business.
Lloyds has no investment banking activities as such in Britain and its senior management has been famously against entering the field, citing the volatility of income from such activities.
